findings.title: Consumer-schema semantics are under-bound
findings.evidence: The authority and preflight bind the Phase-B files by digest, but do not independently assert the accepted aggregate binding, structural dimensions/counts, or five-state T5 availability vocabulary.
findings.why_it_matters: Correct bytes are necessary but not sufficient. A future executor could load the right file while interpreting state codes, axes, or expected dimensions incorrectly. Stage 4 is irreversible once correspondence is opened.

findings.title: Stage-4 authority producer lacks post-commit Git-blob binding
findings.evidence: V64_STAGE4_EXECUTION_AUTHORITY_V1.json records producer path and SHA-256 but no producer Git blob, while its repo-resident input policy otherwise distinguishes committed blob identity from external byte custody.
findings.why_it_matters: This repeats a provenance class already exposed at B6: a producer cannot know its final blob pre-commit, so the post-commit source identity should be bound explicitly rather than inferred later.
